question: When is an off-policy confidence-sequence target actually the same scientific quantity as the role-local predictable-weight reliability target, and what goes wrong if a current-outcome-dependent realized weight is substituted?

public_sources.title: Off-Policy Confidence Sequences
public_sources.relevance: OPE targets the value of a target policy under data generated by a logging policy and uses martingale confidence sequences valid under arbitrary stopping.

public_sources.title: Anytime-valid off-policy inference for contextual bandits
public_sources.relevance: Extends anytime-valid OPE to adaptive logging and time-varying/counterfactual policy-value targets; this is still a counterfactual policy-value contract, not a license to reinterpret arbitrary predictable or realized weights.

matched_special_case.condition: Target policy equals the logging policy exactly, so every importance ratio is identically 1. With unit predictable weights, the IPS/OPE point estimate and the ordinary average-conditional-mean estimator are pathwise identical.
matched_special_case.lesson: This is a legitimate head-to-head only because the estimands coincide. It does not imply a general OPE confidence sequence and a predictable-weight reliability confidence sequence are interchangeable.

wrong_target_realized_weight_counterexam.construction: Let the process-level mismatch Y be Bernoulli(0.05). After Y is realized, assign realized completed count N=10 when Y=1 and N=100 when Y=0, then incorrectly use N as if it were a predictable exposure weight.
wrong_target_realized_weight_counterexam.lesson: The realized current-outcome-dependent weight changes the estimand by nearly an order of magnitude in this example. Knowing the weight before later analysis does not retroactively make it predictable before the current outcome.

boundary_rules: Use OPE when the scientific question is a counterfactual target-policy value under a logging policy and the OPE assumptions/importance-ratio construction are appropriate.
Use predictable process/exposure weights when the scientific question is how actually observed reliability is averaged and those weights are frozen before the current outcome.
A numerical coincidence between two estimators in a special case is not evidence that the underlying estimands are generally the same.
Do not plug outcome-dependent realized completion count into the predictable-weight envelope and call the result planned-exposure reliability.
scope_guards: The matched synthetic case is deliberately a special target=logging case; it is not a benchmark of statistical efficiency between the published OPE method and the role-local confidence sequence.
The counterexample demonstrates target shift, not failure of published OPE methods.
No O, downstream state, other-worker state, or legacy research was used.
